He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined.

In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.
In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.
十年…復為尚書右僕射 again has Right; idiomatic Left repeats the same side error.
In the tenth year he was again made Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.
In the tenth year he was again made Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.
Literal likewise misrenders 右僕射 as Left; the proposed Right matches the Chinese.
In the twelfth year he retired and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with recording duties, retaining his attendant status.
In the twelfth year he retired and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, retaining his attendant status.
Local 金紫光錄大夫 is the standard office 金紫光祿大夫; CText transmits 光祿, and 'with recording duties' invents a separate sense from 錄 that the title does not carry.
In the twelfth year he retired from office and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with recording duties, retaining his attendant status.
In the twelfth year he retired from office and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, retaining his attendant status.
Literal 'recording duties' depends on the same false reading of 錄 in the title; removing it restores the ordinary Grand Master title (光祿).
Header 子 靈符 marks Son Lingfu; 弟 in the following narrative is Lingfu as younger brother of Shanshi, not a correction of this header.
Literal Younger brother contradicts 子; Son: Lingfu parallels 子 山士.

His son Shanshi rose through eminent posts to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Kuaiji. Because his younger brother, Master of Coaches Dao Rang, had coerced and seized children of good families, Shanshi was reduced to administering the commandery in plain clothes.

His son Shanshi rose through eminent posts to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Kuaiji. Because his younger brother, Gentleman of the Coach Bureau Dao Rang, had coerced and seized children of good families, Shanshi was reduced to administering the commandery in plain clothes.
駕部郎 is the Coach Bureau gentleman (郎), not a 'Master of Coaches'; the proposed office title matches the Chinese.
諡曰定子 is the full posthumous name Dingzi; omitting 子 as mere Ding drops part of the title.
Same omission in the literal field: 定子 must be rendered Dingzi in full.
